inspector.bone.autoRigTip: Generates bones, IK chains and controllers scaled to this layer. Replaces any existing rig.
inspector.bone.chainModeTip: IK poses the chain from its goal; FK poses it from the bones. Switching preserves the pose.
inspector.bone.clickToDraw: Click the layer to draw bones.
inspector.bone.noControllers: Add a handle to pose a bone or an IK goal without grabbing the joint.
inspector.bone.noInfluence: No bone reaches this vertex — it stays in its bind position.
inspector.bone.onlyInfluence: is the only influence here, so it holds 100%. Paint a second bone onto this vertex to divide it.
inspector.bone.poleTip: The side the joint bends toward. Without a pole the solver only preserves the current side and can never flip it.
inspector.bone.puppetToo: This layer also has puppet pins — the two rigs compose: the puppet refines the mesh first, then the skeleton pose carries it. The skinning mesh below follows the puppet's mesh settings.
inspector.bone.softnessTip: Pixels over which the limb eases into full reach, so the joint never snaps straight. 0 = off.
inspector.bone.staleVertex: Vertex {n} is from a different mesh resolution. Re-pick a vertex on the canvas.
inspector.bone.stretchTip: How far the limb may lengthen to reach its goal: 1.5 = up to 150 %. 0 = never.
inspector.bone.total: Total {n}%. Editing one weight redistributes the rest in proportion.
inspector.camera.addPoiTip: Make this a two-node camera: it always aims at a Point of Interest, so moving it re-frames the target. Keyframe the point to lead a shot across the scene.
inspector.camera.advancedTip: Aperture: the blur as a lens opening in px — the twin of Blur Level in After Effects.
inspector.camera.bokehTip: The shape of out-of-focus highlights. Iris Blades 0 is a Gaussian blur; 5–11 gives an iris-shaped bokeh with its own roundness, rotation, aspect, fringe and highlight bloom.
inspector.camera.classicTip: Classic: a symmetric blur ramp around the focus plane that ignores focal length (the After Effects look).
inspector.camera.dofTip: Blur layers by their distance from the focus plane. Layers must be 3D.
inspector.camera.filmSizeTip: Film Size is the virtual sensor width. It changes the millimetre reading only — the view itself is set by Zoom / Angle of View.
inspector.camera.irisBladesTip: Leave at 0 for a Gaussian blur. Set 5–11 for an iris-shaped bokeh.
inspector.camera.no3dLayers: No 3D layers — the camera moves nothing yet
inspector.camera.orbitTip: Swings the camera around its point of interest, keeping it framed (Orbit Yaw / Pitch). The viewer's Orbit tool and Alt+drag write these. On canvas: Alt+drag orbits, Shift+Alt+drag (or Alt+middle-drag) tracks XY, Alt+wheel dollies.
inspector.camera.physicalTip: Physical: thin-lens defocus — the foreground blurs harder than the background, distant layers stop getting blurrier, and focal length affects depth of field.
inspector.camera.removePoiTip: Make this a one-node camera: it stops aiming at a target and looks where it is turned
inspector.camera.resetTip: Back to the default framing: the comp centre, pulled back by the focal length so the comp plane renders 1:1, no orbit
inspector.camera.threeDLayersTip: The camera moves layers with the 3D switch on (also per layer in the timeline's switch column). Position and Z live in Transform; a shorter focal length gives a wider, more dramatic perspective.
inspector.camera.turnTip: Turns the camera on the spot without moving it — a tripod pan or tilt (X / Y / Z Rotation). No viewer tool writes these. On a two-node camera they offset the tracked aim, so it keeps following its Point of Interest while looking off to the side.
inspector.cameraShake.hint: Handheld shake the engine adds after the camera's aim: seeded smooth noise, deterministic for a seed. Keyframe Amount to ramp it in or out; camera motion blur sees it.
inspector.cameraShake.newSeedHint: Pick a different random pattern — same strength, new motion
inspector.cameraShake.offHint: Turn the shake off (back to no stored shake)
inspector.cameraShot.addRigHint: Build a crane, dolly or orbit rig of 3D nulls above this camera — then operate it from Camera Rig

stores.onboarding.addShape.body: Pick a shape and drag it out on the canvas. Q cycles rectangle, ellipse and polygon; G does the same for the pen tools next door.
stores.onboarding.addShape.hint: Draw a shape on the canvas to continue.
stores.onboarding.addShape.missing: The toolbar is hidden — reopen it from View, then come back.
stores.onboarding.addShape.title: Draw something
stores.onboarding.export.body: Export writes video, image sequences, GIF and Lottie, and queues long renders in the background so you can keep working. That is the tour — everything else is discoverable from the command palette.
stores.onboarding.export.missing: Export also lives in the File menu.
stores.onboarding.export.title: Get it out
stores.onboarding.fit.body: Semicolon zooms the timeline to the whole composition; Alt+; fits the work area. The zoom cluster in the status bar does the same by mouse.
stores.onboarding.fit.missing: The zoom cluster lives in the status bar under the timeline.
stores.onboarding.fit.title: ; fits the view
stores.onboarding.graphEditor.body: Easing is the difference between "it moved" and "it feels right". The easing pills set a curve in one click; the graph editor lets you draw the curve yourself, with real bezier handles and numeric velocity.
stores.onboarding.graphEditor.hint: Open the graph editor (Shift+F3) to see the curve.
stores.onboarding.graphEditor.missing: The timeline is closed — reopen it to reach the graph editor.
stores.onboarding.graphEditor.title: Shape how it moves
stores.onboarding.inspector.body: The inspector is the layer, in full: transform, fills, effects, 3D. Every number here is a scrubbable slider AND a field that does maths — drag it, or click and type 960/2.
stores.onboarding.inspector.missing: The inspector is collapsed — reopen it with the right-hand panel toggle.
stores.onboarding.inspector.title: Everything about that layer
stores.onboarding.jkl.body: In the timeline J and K hop between keyframes. In the Source Monitor they are the editor’s shuttle: J plays backwards, L forwards, again for 2× and 4×, K stops. Space still plays the comp.
stores.onboarding.jkl.hint: Press Space (or L in the Source Monitor) to play.
stores.onboarding.jkl.title: J, K and L
stores.onboarding.missing.timeline: The timeline is closed — reopen it with the bottom panel toggle.
stores.onboarding.palette.body: Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+P opens the command palette: every command, panel, preset and doc section, searchable. Type ? for the shortcut list.
stores.onboarding.palette.missing: The palette also opens from View ▸ Command Palette.
stores.onboarding.palette.title: Everything, by name
stores.onboarding.play.body: Spacebar, or the button in the middle of the transport. The first pass renders and caches; the second is real time.
stores.onboarding.play.missing: The transport lives under the viewport — reopen the viewport to see it.
stores.onboarding.play.title: Play it
stores.onboarding.powerTour.description: JKL, U / UU, ; to fit, quick apply with + and the command palette.
stores.onboarding.powerTour.label: Power-user Tour
stores.onboarding.quickApply.body: Hover a preset and press + (or click its plus) to drop it on the selected layers at the playhead, without leaving the panel. Drag it onto the canvas to aim it at one layer.
stores.onboarding.quickApply.missing: Open the Presets panel (Window ▸ Presets) to see quick apply.
stores.onboarding.quickApply.title: Quick apply with +
stores.onboarding.reveal.body: Select a layer and press U: every animated property unfolds and everything else stays out of the way. Press U twice quickly (UU) for only the properties you changed from their defaults.
stores.onboarding.reveal.title: U shows what moves
stores.onboarding.secondKeyframe.body: Drag the playhead somewhere later, then change the value. A second keyframe lands automatically, and the two of them are the animation.
stores.onboarding.secondKeyframe.hint: Move the playhead, then change the value you just keyed.
stores.onboarding.secondKeyframe.title: Now make it move
stores.onboarding.setKeyframe.body: A stopwatch turns a property into an animation. Click the one beside Position in the timeline and the current value becomes your first keyframe.
stores.onboarding.setKeyframe.hint: Click any property stopwatch to record a keyframe.
stores.onboarding.setKeyframe.title: Set a keyframe
stores.onboarding.threeD.body: Flip a layer to 3D and it gains Z, orientation and a place in a lit scene. This cluster is how you fly around it: orbit, pan and dolly, the gizmo mode, and which axes it aligns to.
stores.onboarding.threeD.missing: The 3D cluster sits in the toolbar — reopen it from View.
stores.onboarding.threeD.title: 3D, when you want it
